entries.reason: the release takes an IOSurface through the same call with a Y-flip argument the public API does not expose, so the public one is a forward and not a second implementation
entries.effect: forwards to -texImageIOSurface:target:internalFormat:width:height:format:type:plane:invert: on the release with the flip off, which is the only value the public API can ask for; the release's own answer is returned unchanged, and if a release ever lacked that call the method answers NO rather than pretending to have uploaded anything
entries.source: the release's own armv7 6.1.3 ObjC metadata read by objc.binary_inventory, which carries -[EAGLContext texImageIOSurface:target:internalFormat:width:height:format:type:plane:invert:] and no eight-argument form; the header of EAGLIOSurface.h in SDK 26.2 for the contract

entries.effect: the value is kept and read back, and setting it YES installs guards that serialise every call which reaches the release's own context through +setCurrentContext:, -renderbufferStorage:fromDrawable: and -presentRenderbuffer: behind a recursive lock of the port's own, one per context, so a context an application declared shared between threads is entered by one thread at a time. With the value left clear nothing is wrapped at all and the release's code runs untouched, and the fact that guards were installed is said once in the log
entries.source: the header of EAGL.h in SDK 26.2 for the contract (ios(7.1), and iOS 7.1 is where the release's own -initWithAPI:sharedWithCompute: appeared beside it); the release's armv7 6.1.3 ObjC metadata for the three entry points that are wrapped
